title: Alexander takes Maracanda
description: Alexander the Great captures the Sogdian capital and spends two years putting down resistance in the region.

title: Afrasiab murals
description: The Sogdian king Varkhuman has a hall painted with ambassadors from China, Korea and other lands, showing Samarkand's place on the Silk Road.

title: Arab conquest of Samarkand
description: Qutayba ibn Muslim takes Samarkand three years after Bukhara, bringing Transoxiana under the caliphate and beginning its conversion to Islam.

title: Bukhara becomes the Samanid capital
description: Ismail Samani becomes ruler of Transoxiana, and under his dynasty Bukhara is a centre of Persian literature and learning.

title: Karakhanids take Bukhara
description: The Turkic Karakhanids occupy the Samanid capital, ending the dynasty and beginning Turkic rule in Transoxiana.

title: Kalyan Minaret
description: The Karakhanid ruler Arslan Khan builds a 46-metre brick minaret that survives the Mongol conquest.

title: Mongols take Bukhara
description: Genghis Khan captures and burns Bukhara and takes Samarkand a month later, destroying the Khwarazmian Empire.

title: Birth of Timur
description: Timur is born near Kesh into the Turco-Mongol Barlas tribe.

title: Timur makes Samarkand his capital
description: After defeating his rival Amir Husayn, Timur becomes ruler of Transoxiana and begins the conquests that build his empire.

title: Death of Timur
description: Timur dies at the start of a campaign against Ming China and is buried in the Gur-e-Amir in Samarkand.

title: Ulugh Beg Observatory
description: Timur's grandson Ulugh Beg builds an observatory whose star catalogue is the most accurate made before the telescope.

title: Ulugh Beg killed
description: The astronomer-ruler is beheaded on the orders of his son, and Timurid power in Transoxiana declines.

title: Uzbeks take Samarkand
description: Muhammad Shaybani conquers the Timurid capital, and the Uzbeks become the rulers of Transoxiana.

title: Khanate of Khiva founded
description: An Uzbek dynasty takes power in Khwarazm and founds a state that lasts until 1920.

title: Khanate of Kokand founded
description: Shahrukh Bey of the Ming tribe breaks away from Bukhara and founds a state in the Fergana Valley.

title: Nader Shah conquers Bukhara and Khiva
description: The Iranian ruler crosses the Amu Darya, makes Bukhara a vassal and takes Khiva.

title: Stoddart and Conolly executed
description: The emir Nasrullah beheads two British officers, an episode of the rivalry between Britain and Russia in Central Asia.

title: Russians take Tashkent
description: General Chernyayev storms the largest city of Central Asia, which becomes the capital of Russian Turkestan.

title: Bukhara becomes a Russian protectorate
description: After Russian troops take Samarkand the emir cedes it and accepts Russian protection.

title: Fall of Khiva
description: Russian columns under Kaufman converge on Khiva, and the khanate becomes a Russian protectorate.

title: Kokand annexed
description: Russia abolishes the Khanate of Kokand and makes the Fergana Valley a province of Turkestan.

title: Andijan uprising
description: Followers of the Sufi leader Dukchi Ishan attack a Russian barracks and are quickly defeated.

title: Kokand Autonomy crushed
description: Forces of the Tashkent Soviet destroy the Muslim-led autonomous government and sack the city, which feeds the Basmachi revolt.

title: Red Army takes Bukhara
description: Troops under Mikhail Frunze storm the city, the last emir flees and a people's soviet republic is proclaimed.

title: Uzbek SSR created
description: The Soviet government redraws Central Asia along national lines and creates Uzbekistan from parts of Turkestan, Bukhara and Khorezm.

title: Tashkent earthquake
description: An earthquake destroys much of the old city and leaves about 300,000 people homeless, and Tashkent is rebuilt as a model Soviet city.

title: Fergana riots
description: Mobs attack Meskhetian Turks in the Fergana Valley, about a hundred people are killed and tens of thousands are evacuated.

title: Independence
description: Uzbekistan declares independence after the failed coup in Moscow, with Islam Karimov as president.

title: Tashkent bombings
description: Six car bombs kill 16 people in an apparent attempt on President Karimov, and the government responds with mass arrests of Islamists.

title: Andijan massacre
description: Troops fire on a crowd of protesters and kill several hundred people by most independent counts.

title: Death of Islam Karimov
description: The president who had ruled since before independence dies and is succeeded by Shavkat Mirziyoyev, who begins to open the country.
